injuries.description: splinter of metal flew off and into his right eye.
source: As his hammer struck one particular wedge a splinter of metal flew off and into his right eye.
injuries.icd_description: Penetrating wound of orbit with or without foreign body

injuries.description: complicated cataract in his eye together with other associated problems.
source: Due to the severity of the injury he developed a complicated cataract in his eye together with other associated problems.
A report of August last year showed that he also had sympathetic ophthalmitis, tractional retinal detachment and traumatic glaucoma.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

injuries.icd_description: Other specified traumatic injury to eyeball

injuries.description: natural cataract in left eye (removed by operation in September 1987), leaving his left eye in a somewhat poorer condition than the right.
source: To add to his miseries his left eye had developed what we might in the circumstances term a natural cataract, which was removed by operation in September 1987, leaving his left eye in a somewhat poorer condition than the right.

manifestations.description: After his discharge from hospital the vision in his right eye was very limited, he being able to make out the fingers of his hand only when six inches away.
By June 1988 he could with that eye see only vague movements.

A re assessment in May last year, i.e. 1990, showed that when assisted by powerful lenses the distant visual acuity in his eye was 6/12, while at close range he ought to have been able to read normal type at a distance of 25 centimeters.
His peripheral vision was also limited.
Left eye in a somewhat poorer condition than the right (after cataract operation in September 1987).

treatments_received: emergency operation at Princess Margaret Hospital
transfer to Queen Elizabeth Hospital and surgical removal of the splinter
follow-up treatment with steroids and antibiotics

losses.description: Loss/impairment of vision in the right eye resulting in very limited vision (able to make out fingers only at six inches), later only vague movements, limited peripheral vision and risk of deterioration.
